Resolution No. 12-03
Withdrawals From Life Membership Funds
The proponents of this Resolution seek to modify how withdrawals are taken from
a Lodge Life Membership Fund.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, we have not been consistent as to the manner and timing of
a Lodge’s withdrawals from a Life Membership Fund pursuant to Section 809.150
of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, there should be a consistent approach to such
withdrawals; and
WHEREAS, some Lodges have not withdrawn the permissible amount
of interest and dividends from the Life Membership Fund on an annual basis; and
WHEREAS, Lodges which have failed to make the permitted
withdrawals should not be penalized if the law in this area is modified.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.150 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:

190

Proceedings of the

§809.150. LIFE MEMBERSHIP FUND.
The original amounts paid for life memberships shall be forever kept and
maintained held as and for a separate and permanent Life Membership Fund. A
Lodge may invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in Section 809.130 of
this Code, if such investments are kept separate and apart from all other Lodge
assets. Only interest or dividends paid in cash on the Life Membership Fund
shall be available for general Lodge use. Interest and dividends received during
a calendar year must be withdrawn on or before December 31st of the following
calendar year. Otherwise, they shall be added to principal and may not thereafter
be withdrawn.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that, if there is any interest or dividends
paid in cash on a Lodge’s Life Membership Fund during the two complete fiscal
years ending prior to the adoption of this Resolution which has not previously
been withdrawn for general Lodge use, the Lodge may withdraw such amounts
for general Lodge use by December 31 of the calendar year of the adoption of
this Resolution.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that, should this resolution and one
or more of Resolutions 12-04, 12-07 and 12-08 be adopted, the modifications of
Section 809.150 of the California Masonic Code as enacted by this Resolution
12-03 shall be repealed.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Seven Resolutions that will be considered during this legislative
session, namely 2012-03 through 2012-09, address aspects of Life Membership.
Resolution 2012-03 is concerned with the definition of what is principal and what
is income in these funds.
While the California Masonic Code permits a Lodge to use the income
from a Life Membership Fund, it cannot use the principal. In practice, a Lodge
could interpret the law to mean that any income in the Life Membership Fund
that is not used in a particular year could be withdrawn from the fund and used
in subsequent years. This Resolution, if adopted, prevents a Lodge that chooses
not to withdraw the full amount of money that is potentially available in the
Lodge’s Life Membership Fund during a particular calendar year from being able
to withdraw that money in future years. The wording that is proposed to be added
to Section 809.150 of the California Masonic Code makes all such unused funds
part of the principal of the Life Membership Fund in perpetuity.
The second part of this Resolution categorizes income that has been
deposited into the fund in the two years prior to the adoption of this Resolution as
a temporary exclusion. Thus, if any of that money has not been used in the past,

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

191

it can be withdrawn prior to December 31 of the year in which the Resolution
is adopted. This part of Resolution 2012-03 provides the Lodge with a final
opportunity to withdraw unused income from the prior two years
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to permit changes and clarifications
in the manner in which Life Membership Funds are administered.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Resolution CARRIED-OVER.
Resolution No. 12-04
Requires Life Membership Funds to be Invested For Total Return and
Establishes Rules For Life Membership Gifts and Contributions
The proponents of this Resolution seek to provide clarity and direction as to how
a Life Membership Fund should be managed.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Section 809.150 of the California Masonic Code
specifically allows a Life Membership Fund to be invested for “total return,” in a
like manner as all other Lodge funds, according to the rules of Section 809.130;
and
WHEREAS, the “interest or dividends paid in cash” clause does not
adequately include all the permissible types of investments and withdrawals as
provided for in Section 809.130 of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, many Lodges are under the incorrect assumption that Life
Membership Funds should be invested only in very safe vehicles such as checking,
savings, money market or certificates of deposit accounts, which do not provide
adequate returns to allow the Fund to keep pace with inflation or provide growth,
let alone replace the dues income from a member or even cover the expenses of
the Grand Lodge Per Capita Tax; and
WHEREAS, the “original amounts . . . shall be forever kept and
maintained” clause was never meant to be an obstacle to prudent investment as
provided for in Section 809.130 of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, “forever kept and maintained” does not require that
investments be made with a guarantee of retaining principal; and
WHEREAS, the idea that the investment of the Life Membership Fund
must be kept separate and apart from all other Lodge assets does not mean that
the fund must be invested differently from other Lodge assets, only that it must be
segregated and invested separately from other Lodge assets; and

192

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, the contract entered into between the purchasing member
and the Lodge at the time of purchase of a life membership is simple: the purchasing
member pays the Lodge a fixed sum and the Lodge promises the purchaser that he
will never again pay dues to that Lodge; and
WHEREAS, the Lodge promises that the member will never again be
required to pay dues in that Lodge even if the assets in the Life Membership Fund
are no longer sufficient to pay his dues.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.150 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.150. LIFE MEMBERSHIP FUND.
The original amounts paid for life memberships shall be forever kept and
maintained as and for a separate and permanent Life Membership Fund. A Lodge
may invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in Section 809.130 of this
Code, if such investments are kept separate and apart from all other Lodge assets.
Only interest or dividends paid in cash on the Life Membership Fund shall be
available for general Lodge use.
A.

All amounts paid for a life membership shall constitute a permanent Life
Membership Fund, which shall be segregated into one or more accounts
which are separate from all other Lodge funds, investments and assets.

B.

A Lodge may only invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in
Section 809.130 of this Code. However, all investments of the Life
Membership Fund described in Section 809.130.B of this Code must
be conservative growth investments which are designed for total return
(defined as any investment returns, including capital gains/appreciation
and losses/depreciation – realized or unrealized – and all dividends
and interest).
A Lodge’s Life Membership Fund may not be used to secure or fund any
loan to a Lodge or Hall Association, nor may it be used as collateral for a
mortgage or promissory note to or for the benefit of any entity or person.

C.

A Lodge may withdraw the income from its Life Membership Fund for
the general use of the Lodge at any time. For this purpose, income means
all interest and dividends received in cash with respect to investments
held as part of the Life Membership Fund. However, no Lodge is
obligated to take withdrawals from its Life Membership Fund. Interest
and dividends received during a calendar year must be withdrawn on or
before December 31st of the following calendar year. Otherwise, they
shall be added to principal and may not thereafter be withdrawn.

D.

A Lodge purchasing a life membership for the retiring Master as
provided in Section 809.550.D of this Code must transfer the total
purchase price of the life membership from its general funds to its Life
Membership Fund.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

193

E.

A life membership may be purchased as a memorial at any time for a
Master Mason who, at the time of his death, was a member in good
standing of the Lodge. The purchase price for such life membership shall
be paid in full at the time of purchase and calculated in accordance with
Section 809.320 of this Code and the current life membership plan of
the Lodge. If a Lodge uses the plan described in Section 809.320.B, the
purchase price shall be calculated by using the age of the member at the
time of his death.

F.

Nothing in this Code shall prevent any person from making voluntary
contributions to the Life Membership Fund.

G.

A Life Membership Fund, once established, may never be dissolved
or combined with general Lodge funds, even if there may be no life
members currently living or if further sales of life memberships have
been discontinued.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 809.320 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.320. LIFE MEMBERSHIP.
A Lodge may adopt a standing resolution providing for a life membership plan,
which shall forever exempt a member making the required payment into the plan
from the payment of dues in the Lodge. The resolution may be adopted, amended
or revoked at any Stated Meeting by a majority vote of the members present.
Any such action must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated Meeting and
written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth the text of the
proposed action and the date of the Stated Meeting at which the vote is to be taken.
The plan must provide that a life membership shall be granted upon payment of:
A.

A sum of money which is not less than 20.83 times the Lodge’s annual
dues at the time of purchase of the life membership; or

B.

A sum of money equal to the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase
of the life membership multiplied by the factor indicated opposite the
member’s age in the following schedule:
Age 49 and under, 21 times annual dues;
50 to 54 inclusive, 19 times annual dues;
55 to 59 inclusive, 17 times annual dues;
60 to 64 inclusive, 14 times annual dues; and
65 and over, 11 times annual dues.

194

Proceedings of the

The resolution shall take effect only upon its approval by the Grand Master.
The Secretary shall send to each life member at his last known address, annually,
a Life Membership Dues Card for the next calendar year.
A life membership is an executed contract requiring the consent of the Lodge and
the life member to rescind it.
The Grand Secretary shall provide the form of contract to be used by the Lodge
when a life membership is purchased (other than as a memorial). Such contract
must be signed by the member for whom the life membership is being purchased,
the Lodge Master and the Lodge Secretary, affixed with the seal of the Lodge. The
original shall be kept as part of the member’s permanent membership record. A
copy of the signed contract shall be provided to the member.
A life member who has been suspended or expelled and who shall thereafter
become restored or elected to membership in a Lodge in which a life membership
was once held shall also be restored as a life member of that Lodge.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to provide clarity and direction
as to how a Life Membership Fund should be purchased, invested and managed.
This Resolution intends to re-write section 809.150 dealing with Life
Membership Funds. This Resolution also intends to amend section 809.320 that
will direct the Grand Secretary to provide the form of contract to be used by the
Lodge when a life membership is purchased.
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to permit changes and clarifications
in the manner in which Life Membership Funds are administered.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

195

This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Investments:
Section 809.150 of the California Masonic Code specifically allows a
Life Membership Fund to be invested for “Total Return,” in a like manner as
all other Lodge funds, according to the rules of Section 809.130. Total Return
is defined as any investment return, including capital gains/appreciation and
losses/depreciation – realized or unrealized – and all dividends and interest. This
resolution clarifies that there is myriad allowable investments in Life Membership
Funds that should be prudently considered within the context of the prevailing
financial markets.
Many Lodges are under the false assumption that Life Membership
Funds should be invested only in investments perceived to be safe vehicles such
as checking, savings, money market or certificates of deposit accounts. These
investments do not provide adequate returns to allow the Life Membership Fund
to keep pace with inflation or provide needed long-term growth of capital.
The “original amounts . . . shall be forever kept and maintained” clause
was never meant to be an obstacle to prudent investment as provided for in
Section 809.130 of the California Masonic Code. “Forever kept and maintained”
does not require that investments be made with a guarantee of retaining principal.
Furthermore, the idea that the investment of the Life Membership Fund must
be kept separate and apart from all other Lodge assets does not mean that the
fund must be invested differently from other Lodge assets, only that it must
be segregated and invested in a separate account that is distinct from other
Lodge assets.
This Resolution simply clarifies, expands and underscores the myriad
prudent investments currently allowed in the California Masonic Code. At the
same time this outlines the potential pitfalls of being too conservative with longterm investments.

Resolution No. 12-05
Transfers Life Membership Fund to the Consolidated Lodge

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the California Masonic Code is silent on the effect of a
consolidation of two or more Lodges as to the Life Membership Funds where the
consolidated Lodge does not have a Life Membership Plan; and
WHEREAS, the California Masonic Code does not specifically provide

§813.010. CONSOLIDATION.
A.

Two or more Lodges, located near each other, may consolidate into one

to be approved by his Lodge. If a Master of a Lodge participating in

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to ensure that if a Lodge which
has a life membership plan consolidates with a Lodge that has no such plan,
the life members of the former Lodge will become life members of the newly
consolidated Lodge, and the newly consolidated Lodge will establish a segregated
account for the Life Membership Funds. This legislation would not require the
newly consolidated Lodge to start or create a new life membership plan for
its members.
Currently, there are provisions made in the California Masonic Code
that protect members with life membership, but there is no mention as to what
would happen to their funds if the newly consolidated Lodge does not have a life
membership plan.
It has long been the policy of this Grand Lodge that the constituent
Lodges segregate, protect and preserve Life Membership Funds. The provisions
of this Resolution extend that policy to ensure that a member’s ‘Life Membership
Funds’ in a newly consolidated Lodge are established, segregated and properly
accounted for.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution 2012-06 clarifies the vested interest that a particular life
member has in his Lodge’s Life Membership Fund. This vested interest is of
particular concern when a Lodge dissolves on its own or has its charter revoked
by Grand Lodge. In such a case, any life member of the disbanded Lodge who was
not a member of another Lodge at that time automatically becomes a member of
the Grand Master’s Lodge. The Life Membership Fund of the Lodge becomes the
property of Grand Lodge. When that man then chooses to join another Lodge, he
would be required either to purchase another life membership if one were to be
available or to start paying annual dues. Thus, through no fault of the member, the
benefit of life membership is lost.
In order to address this situation, the proponents of Resolution 2012-06
have created a definition of a member’s “vested interest.” This would represent
the amount of money that would be transferred to the new Lodge by Grand Lodge
as credit against the purchase of another life membership. If the member joining
the new Lodge just chooses to pay annual dues, no credit for the previous life
membership would be available.
Section 809.320 currently states that life membership is a contract
between a Lodge and a member that requires the consent of both in order for it
to be rescinded. Resolution 2012-06 expands on that principle by identifying the
amount of money that is due the member who is a party in such a rescission. In
such a case, the member would be entitled to a return of his vested interest.
The member’s vested interest in the Life Membership Fund is to
be defined as the lesser of two figures, namely the amount of money that the
member originally paid for the Life Membership or the fair market value of that
membership at the current time.
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to permit changes and clarifications
in the manner in which Life Membership Funds are administered.
The Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, it has long been the policy of this Grand Lodge to invest
the funds of the Grand Lodge of California in conservative investment instruments
and to allow its constituent Lodges to invest their funds in like manner; and
WHEREAS, the Grand Lodge of California and its various entities
– including the Masonic Homes of California and the California Masonic
Foundation – invest their funds conservatively for total return; and
WHEREAS, conservative investments yield conservative, reliable and
profitable returns which allow for growth and inflation when prudently managed
over a long-term investment strategy; and
WHEREAS, it is desirable for Lodges to develop a long-term investment
strategy for their Life Membership Funds to keep pace with annual dues, pay the
Grand Lodge Per Capita Tax, account for inflation and provide for growth; and
WHEREAS, it is reasonable that a Lodge should be able to budget its
income from investments based on a steady percentage rather than the unknown
amount of dividends and interest which can vary widely.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.150 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.150. LIFE MEMBERSHIP FUND.
The original amounts paid for life memberships shall be forever kept and
maintained as and for a separate and permanent Life Membership Fund. A Lodge
may invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in Section 809.130 of this
Code, if such investments are kept separate and apart from all other Lodge assets.
Only interest or dividends paid in cash on the Life Membership Fund shall be
available for general Lodge use.
A.

All amounts paid for a life membership shall constitute a permanent Life
Membership Fund, which shall be segregated into one or more accounts
which are separate from all other Lodge funds, investments and assets.

B.

A Lodge may only invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in
Section 809.130 of this Code. However, all investments of the Life
Membership Fund described in Section 809.130.B of this Code must
be conservative growth investments which are designed for total return
(defined as any investment returns, including capital gains/appreciation
and losses/depreciation – realized or unrealized – and all dividends
and interest).
A Lodge’s Life Membership Fund may not be used to secure or fund any
loan to a Lodge or Hall Association, nor may it be used as collateral for a
mortgage or promissory note to or for the benefit of any entity or person.

206
C.

Proceedings of the
A Lodge may make withdrawals from its Life Membership Fund for the
general use of the Lodge in the following manner only:
1.

The December 31st value of the Lodge’s Life Membership Fund
for each of the prior three years shall be averaged together. The
maximum allowable withdrawal during the calendar year shall
be 4.0% of that averaged value, except as follows:
a.

If the Life Membership Fund of a Lodge has existed
for less than three complete calendar years, but for at
least one complete calendar year, the December 31st
value for each year in which the Fund was in existence
shall be averaged together. The maximum allowable
withdrawal during the calendar year shall be 4.0% of
that averaged value; and

b.

If the Life Membership Fund of a Lodge was created
in the prior calendar year, the maximum allowable
withdrawal during the calendar year shall be 4.0%
of the value on December 31st of the prior calendar
year; and

c.

If the Life Membership Fund of a Lodge was created
during the current calendar year, no withdrawals may
be made during the calendar year;

2.

Lodge withdrawals from its Life Membership Fund during each
calendar year may be made in one or more increments, provided
that the total withdrawal for the calendar year does not exceed
the maximum allowable withdrawal as calculated in paragraph
1 above. If a Lodge fails to withdraw any or all of the amount to
which it would have otherwise been entitled during a calendar
year, then it shall be prohibited from taking that withdrawal in
any subsequent year; and

3.

Permissible withdrawals under this section shall be transferred
to the Lodge’s bank or other investment accounts for the general
use of the Lodge.

The Grand Secretary shall provide the Lodges with a form which may be
used to make the calculations described above.
No Lodge is obligated to take withdrawals from its Life
Membership Fund.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clarify how each Lodge may
invest its Life Membership Fund for total return and withdrawal annually of
up to four percent of the three year average fund balance. This proposal would
also clarify the definition of investments which may be unclear in the California
Masonic Code at the present. This revision provides that all investments of the
Life Membership Fund as described in section 809.130 must be conservative
growth investments which are designed for total return (defined as any investment
returns, including capital gains/appreciation and losses/depreciation - realized or
unrealized - and all dividends and interest).
The proponents also highly encourage Lodges to develop a long-term
investment strategy for their Life Membership Fund to keep pace with annual
dues, pay the Grand Lodge Per Capita Tax, account for inflation and provide for
growth in the Fund over the long term.
The proponents of this Resolution recognize that interest or dividends,
may not be sufficient for the maintenance of the Lodge for general Lodge
use, particularly in the periods of financial uncertainty. The proposed revision
of California Masonic Code section 809.150 would allow the Lodge to know
specifically, at the start of the Masonic Year, how much money would be available
from the Life Membership Fund. This rate is the same as Grand Lodge employs.
This Resolution does not change the provision that a Lodge may never
access the original amounts paid for life memberships.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Investments:
This Resolution underscores the importance of investing Life Membership
Funds for long-term growth of capital. This is consistent with Section 809.130.B
of the Code, which states that investments must be made in conservative growth
investments that are designed for total return.
Total Return is defined as any investment returns, including capital gains/
appreciation and losses/depreciation – realized or unrealized – and all dividends
and interest. This resolution clarifies that there is myriad allowable investments in
Life Membership Funds that should be prudently considered within the context of
the prevailing financial markets.

208

Proceedings of the

While the resolution does not require a lodge to make annual
withdrawals, it does limit the annual withdrawals to 4% of the rolling three-year
average. There is no make-up provision for missed distributions. The Investment
Committee believes this is prudent investment practice as it allows the corpus
of the Life Membership Fund to grow over time without aggressively drawing
down principle.

Resolution No. 12-08
Gives a Lodge the Option to Request That Grand Lodge Invest and
Administer Its Life Membership Fund
The proponents of this Resolution seek to give each Lodge the option of having
the Grand Lodge invest and administer that Lodge’s Life Membership Fund.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the Investment Committee of the Grand Lodge of
California is well-versed in the types of available investment instruments which
are allowable under the rules of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, some Lodges are not comfortable with all of the intricacies
and variables related to a detailed knowledge of investments; and
WHEREAS, some Lodges desire assistance or would prefer to not to be
responsible for investing the funds of a Life Membership Fund; and
WHEREAS, the Investment Committee and the Grand Secretary’s
Office of the Grand Lodge of California are willing and able to administer and
invest Life Membership Funds for any Lodge requesting it; and
WHEREAS, other Grand Lodge Jurisdictions successfully provide for a
Life Membership Fund administered by their Grand Lodge.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.110 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.110. POWER AND CONTROL OVER LODGE ASSETS.
A Lodge must retain control of and hold title to keep all monies, property and
other assets of the Lodge with the power to acquire, mortgage, sell and convey
property and to invest and reinvest its funds, except as follows:

A.

All amounts paid for a life membership shall constitute a permanent Life

A Lodge may only invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in

Lodge shall note in the minutes of the Lodge the notice of the proposed
action when made. When transmitting the action for approval, he shall
forward a certificate, under seal, showing that the law has been complied
with and that the action has received the required vote.

No Lodge shall be required to participate in a Life Membership Fund
administered by the Grand Lodge.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to give each Lodge the option of
having the Grand Lodge invest and administer that Lodge’s Life Membership Fund
by amending section 809.110 of our Code. This Resolution also intends to amend
section 809.150 to define rules for “Life Membership Gifts and Contributions.”
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to permit changes and clarifications
in the manner in which Life Membership Funds are administered. It also has long
been the policy of this Grand Lodge to offer assistance to constituent Lodges
when asked.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Investments:
The committee finds the resolution to be favorable for lodges and notes
the following advantages:
•

Quality of Money Managers

•

Cost

•

Ease of burden

1.

Quality of Money Managers: Grand Lodge currently manages over $700
Million for Grand Lodge and related entities. The size of the portfolio
gives Grand Lodge access to the very best institutional money managers
that would not ordinarily be available to smaller sized investors. Lodges
would benefit by gaining access to those same money managers.

2.

Cost: Piggybacking on the Grand Lodge investment portfolio also offers
access to money managers at very favorable fees. This should allow
most lodges to reduce their investment costs considerably.

3.

Ease of Burden: Lodges that choose to have Grand Lodge invest their
Life Membership assets would eliminate the administrative burden of
(1st) choosing the investments (2nd) monitoring the performance (3rd)
accounting for the annual distribution of “Interest & Dividends”. The
Grand Lodge Finance Committee would maintain separate accounting
for each lodge’s funds and facilitate the distribution at year-end. No
administrative cost for these services will be passed on to the respective
individual lodges.

This Resolution does not relinquish power or control of Life Membership
funds to Grand Lodge. It simply allows a lodge to retain Grand Lodge to invest
and administer its Life Membership Fund on behalf of the Lodge, as provided in
Section 809.150. This arrangement can be terminated at any time by majority vote
of the Lodge.

Resolution No. 12-09
Allows a Member to Transfer His Life Membership
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow the transfer of a life membership
between two Constituent Lodges.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, it is unfair that dues-paying members of a Lodge may
transfer their memberships to another Lodge in this Jurisdiction without penalty,
but life members who wish to do so would be penalized by either having to
resume paying dues in his new Lodge or purchase another life membership in his
new Lodge; and
WHEREAS, the purpose of a life membership often is to avoid paying
dues thereafter; and
WHEREAS, in today’s mobile society it is not unusual for members to
relocate to an area which is a long distance from their Lodge and they desire to be
a member in the new area; and
WHEREAS, transferability would not be detrimental to the Lodge to
which a member wishes to transfer; and
WHEREAS, a refund of life membership dues is not available now
upon transferring to another Lodge.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that section 809.320 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.320. LIFE MEMBERSHIP.
A Lodge may adopt a standing resolution providing for a life membership plan,
which shall forever exempt a member making the required payment into the plan
from the payment of dues in the Lodge. The resolution may be adopted, amended
or revoked at any Stated Meeting by a majority vote of the members present.
Any such action must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated Meeting and

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

215

written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth the text of the
proposed action and the date of the Stated Meeting at which the vote is to be taken.
The plan must provide that a life membership shall be granted upon payment of:
A.

A sum of money which is not less than 20.83 times the Lodge’s annual
dues at the time of purchase of the life membership; or

B.

A sum of money equal to the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase
of the life membership multiplied by the factor indicated opposite the
member’s age in the following schedule:
Age 49 and under, 21 times annual dues;
50 to 54 inclusive, 19 times annual dues;
55 to 59 inclusive, 17 times annual dues;
60 to 64 inclusive, 14 times annual dues; and
65 and over, 11 times annual dues.

The resolution shall take effect only upon its approval by the Grand Master.
The Secretary shall send to each life member at his last known address, annually,
a Life Membership Dues Card for the next calendar year.
A life membership is an executed contract requiring the consent of the Lodge and
the life member to rescind it. A life member has no interest in the Lodge’s Life
Membership Fund, except in the case of a rescission of his life membership with
his consent and the consent of the Lodge or as elsewhere provided in this Code.
Any other provision of this Code to the contrary notwithstanding, a life member
of a Constituent Lodge who is a member of another Constituent Lodge which then
offers life memberships may elect to transfer his interest in the first Lodge Life
Membership Fund to the Life Membership Fund of the second Lodge. The life
member’s interest in the first Lodge’s Life Membership Fund shall be equal to the
lesser of the original sum of money paid to purchase his life membership or his
share of the fair market value of such Lodge’s Life Membership Fund at the time
of his election to membership in the second Lodge, as determined by the Grand
Treasurer. In making this determination, the Grand Treasurer shall compute the
interest of each living life member in the first Lodge’s Life Membership Fund and
the interest of the first Lodge in it, on a just and equitable basis. If such member’s
interest in the first Lodge’s Life Membership Fund is less than the current cost
of a life membership in the second Lodge, he must pay the difference within 60
days of the notice of its determination in order for the transfer of that amount to
be effective.

216

Proceedings of the

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that, should two or all of Resolutions
12-04, 12-06 and 12-09 be adopted, the Committee on Jurisprudence be authorized
to arrange Section 809.320 of the California Masonic Code by paragraphs and
subparagraphs, lettered and numbered as appropriate, as and to the extent that the
committee shall determine.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow the transfer of a Life
Membership between two Constituent Lodges. Presently it is not possible to
transfer such membership so life members who wish to do so would be penalized
by either having to resume paying dues in his new Lodge or purchase another life
membership in his new Lodge. The proponents propose a procedure whereby the
transfer of membership may be made.
Today, we have a very mobile society so it is not unusual for members
to relocate to an area which may be a considerable distance from their Lodge, and
they are desirous in becoming a member in their new area. This proposal provides
the procedure by which he may do so along with the understanding of what the
transferring member must pay if his interest in the first Lodge’s Life Membership
Fund is less than the current cost of a life membership in the second Lodge.
However, this proposed legislation would permit a member to
unilaterally transfer his life membership without the consent of his Lodge. The
life membership is a contract between the member and his Lodge and it takes both
parties to a contract to effect a rescission. In addition, once a life membership is
purchased the funds belong to the Lodge in perpetuity and the member has no
interest therein.
This Resolution is not consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Resolution CARRIED-OVER.
Resolution No. 12-10
Modifies Rules on Masonic Organizations
The proponents of this Resolution seek to make Section 1200.015 of the California
Masonic Code consistent with its original intent.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Section 1200.015 of the California Masonic Code does not
currently reflect the original intent of the provision, as set forth in Section 332.1
of the 1956 California Masonic Code; and

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

217

WHEREAS, Section 1200.015 of the California Masonic Code does
not currently reflect the interpretations of Section 332.1 of the 1956 California
Masonic Code made by Grand Master Leo E. Anderson which were approved by
Grand Lodge in 1958; and
WHEREAS, Section 1200.015 of the California Masonic Code should
reflect its original intent; and
WHEREAS, Section 1200.015 of the California Masonic Code should
reflect how it has been interpreted since its adoption.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that section 1200.015 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1200.015. MEMBERSHIP IN MASONIC ORGANIZATIONS.
Except as provided below, a Mason residing in this Jurisdiction shall not be,
become or remain a member of any Masonic Organization with activities in this
Jurisdiction, unless:
A.

The Masonic Organization existed was established or organized in this
Jurisdiction on September 27, 1957; or

B.

The Constitution and Bylaws of the Masonic Organization have
first been submitted to Grand Lodge for approval at a subsequent
Annual Communication.

This section shall not be construed as a recognition of any organization whether
or not in existence on September 27, 1957; nor shall it be construed as prohibiting
clubs organized for the purpose of instituting a new Lodge. This section shall
not apply to organizations or associations composed exclusively of Past Masters,
Masters and/or Wardens of a Constituent Lodge or Constituent Lodges. This
section shall not apply to Masonic Organizations which do not confer degrees and,
except for ceremonies of installation, do not have a ritual other than the Ritual of
this Jurisdiction. This section shall not apply to any group, chapter, order, club,
association or organization established or organized by or under the control of a
Masonic Organization which was established or organized in this Jurisdiction on
September 27, 1957.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to revise Code section 1200.015
to make it more consistent with its original intent when that section was adopted
in 1956. Our Code has made it clear, from the beginning, that any organization
which requires its members to be Masons must have the approval of the Grand
Lodge of California. What might not have been clear is that Masons moving into

218

Proceedings of the

this jurisdiction who have membership in Masonic organizations that have not
been approved by this Grand Lodge must drop out of that organization. The intent
of the proponents is to clarify the law by making it more specific that a Mason
cannot be a member of such an organization even if he was a member before
coming to California.
This Resolution further clarifies that membership in organizations which
have been recognized in this jurisdiction is not affected by this law. To give but
one example: the Shrine is a recognized organization, and because it is, any club
or group affiliated with the Shrine does not need separate recognition by our
Grand Lodge.
This Resolution is consistent with the policies and general purpose of
this Grand Lodge.
Resolution ADOPTED.
Resolution No. 12-11
Modifies Amount of Back Dues Payable on Restoration
The proponents of this Resolution seek to give a Lodge the discretion to set the
amount of dues payable by a Master Mason seeking restoration if he has not paid
them or had them remitted by his Lodge for a period of two years.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, if a member has been suspended for two years or more and
seeks restoration, he must pay all dues accrued when he was suspended as well as
all dues which would have accrued had he not been suspended, unless remitted by
his Lodge, and remissions are only allowed based on need; and
WHEREAS, the old Secretary’s Manual provided that the Lodge had
discretion in setting this amount; and
WHEREAS, the proponents believe that a rule more closely following
that set forth in the old Secretary’s Manual is more appropriate.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that section 809.380 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.380. RESTORATION OF A MEMBER SUSPENDED FOR NONPAYMENT OF DUES.
A member suspended for non-payment of dues:

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

219

A.

Shall be automatically restored if, within two years, he pays any arrearage
due at the time of his suspension, together with such further dues as
would have accrued against him had he not been suspended, to the date
of his payment, unless such arrearage and dues have been remitted by his
Lodge; and

B.

May make a request to his Lodge for restoration if he has not paid them
or had them remitted by his Lodge for the period of two years. The
member shall not be restored except by a two-thirds vote by ballot of
all the members present at the next Stated Meeting after the request for
restoration is presented. As a condition of his restoration, he shall pay
such amount of any arrearage due at the time of his suspension, together
with and such amount of such further dues as would have accrued against
him had he not been suspended, to the date of his payment, as his Lodge
may require, unless the except such arrearage and dues that have been
remitted by his Lodge. A petition denied may be renewed at any future
Stated Meeting.

The Secretary shall immediately notify the Grand Secretary of the restoration.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to give a Lodge the discretion to
set the amount of dues payable by a Master Mason seeking restoration if he has
not paid them or had them remitted by his Lodge for a period of two years.
This Resolution continues the procedure for each Lodge to restore
suspended members by having the member pay the delinquent dues as of the
time of suspension. This Resolution then provides each Lodge the flexibility of
charging the member any amount of the dues that would have accrued since the
suspension, which potentially may be nothing for one member and the full amount
for another. This Resolution would allow a Lodge to charge different amounts of
back dues, even if the periods of suspension were the same.
Current practice permits a Lodge to determine the amount of back dues
any particular member must pay and this Resolution codifies that practice.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Resolution ADPOPTED.

Resolution No. 12-12
Cleans Up and Clarifies Portions of the California Masonic Code

The proponents of this Resolution seek to clean up and clarify portions of the
California Masonic Code.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Fourth Edition of the California Masonic Code became
effective at the close of the 2006 Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge on
October 11, 2006; and
WHEREAS, since then, users of the Fourth Edition have identified a
number of places where the language of the Fourth Edition should be cleaned-up
or clarified; and
WHEREAS, this resolution addresses those places found since the
adoption of Resolution 11-03.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that 30.000 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§30.000. AUTHORITY.
A.

Grand Lodge is the supreme Masonic power and authority in the State
of California and is vested with all legislative, executive, and judicial
powers in furtherance of same, limited only by a strict adherence to the
Ancient Landmarks, by the other General Regulations of Masonry and
by the provisions of this Constitution and any other laws and regulations
as it may enact or amend from time to time;

B.

The Jurisdiction of Grand Lodge includes all Lodges, Masons, Masonic
Organizations, their members, Masonic Youth Orders, their members
and advisors and Masonic activities in the State of California and other
states or territories where no recognized Grand Lodge exists, and all
Lodges and their members Masons outside of this state, acting under
its authority, and members Masons of Constituent Lodges wherever
residing; and

C.

Grand Lodge alone has authority to charter or grant dispensations for a
Masonic Lodge in this Jurisdiction.

Grand Lodge may waive its right to maintain exclusive authority and jurisdiction
in the State of California and permit concurrent jurisdiction with other Grand
Bodies; provided such waiver is adopted in the same manner that amendments
may be made to this Constitution.

Resolution No. 12-14
WITHDRAWN
Resolution No. 12-15
Stops the Practice of Closing the Preparation Room Door on a Newly Obligated
Brother Upon His Readmission Into the Lodge
The proponents of this Resolution seek to stop the practice of closing the
preparation room door on a newly obligated Brother upon his readmission into
the Lodge.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, let it be known that the door of Freemasonry should always
remain open to a brother; and

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

231

WHEREAS, in the First and Second Degree the Senior Deacon answers
the alarm at the door of the preparation room in the second section of those
degrees; and
WHEREAS, after opening the door for a newly obligated brother(s), the
Senior Deacon then closes the door to announce the brother(s) to the Worshipful
Master; and
WHEREAS, the Worshipful Master then admits the brother to the
Lodge, and the Senior Deacon is instructed to re-open the door to admit the new
brother; and
WHEREAS, a change in our ceremonies is now appropriate and
desirable for consistency with our principle of not closing the door of the Lodge
on a brother.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Ritual of the
Entered Apprentice and Fellow Craft Degrees be amended as follows:
The preparation room door shall be left open after the Senior Deacon answers
the alarm for the admission of the newly obligated brother and while the Senior
Deacon reports the cause of the alarm to the Worshipful Master, and not closed
until the newly obligated brother has been admitted.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Committee on Ritual be
authorized to make any changes it deems necessary in the cipher ritual to effect
these changes.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to modify the current ritual in the
second section of the Entered Apprentice and Fellow Craft degrees by requiring
that the door to the preparation room remain open while the Senior Deacon informs
the Worshipful Master that the newly-obligated brother desires admission.
The rationale for making this change in our ritual is stated by the
proponents as “consistency with our principle of not closing the door of the Lodge
on a brother.”
No such principle exists in our ritual. For example, when a brother desires
admission to a tiled Lodge meeting, he informs the Tyler who then knocks at the
door, which is opened by the Junior Deacon. After the Junior Deacon is informed
of the brother’s desire for admission, the door is closed and the Worshipful Master
informed. Only after the Worshipful Master approves the request for admission
does the Junior Deacon open the door and permit the brother to enter the Lodge.
This procedure implies no disrespect to the brother seeking admission but is an
affirmation of the Master’s authority over the Lodge and is followed regardless of
whether the brother is a newly-obligated Mason or the Grand Master.

232

Proceedings of the

Resolutions 89-04, 91-14, and 03-08 proposed changing the ritual
for the beginning of the second section of the Entered Apprentice and Fellow
Craft Degrees and were not adopted. In its report to the Grand Lodge in 2003 on
Resolution 03-08, this Committee stated that, “It is not the policy of this Grand
Lodge to legislate changes in the ritual that make no difference in its intent.”
Also, in its report to the Grand Lodge in 2011, this Committee stated
that, “One of the beauties of Freemasonry is the continuity of its traditions and
ritual, stretching back in an unbroken chain to its earliest years. Changes in that
ritual should be made only for the most important reasons and then only after
thorough review.”
This Resolution is not consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Ritual:
The proponents of this resolution seek to modify the ritual by ceasing the
practice of closing the door of the lodge on a newly obligated Brother until he is
admitted into the Lodge.
At the 1989 and 1997 Annual Communication, you considered, and
rejected, a resolution much the same as this, in which the proponent was afraid
the candidate would somehow be offended when the preparation room door was
closed after requesting admission at the opening of the second section of the 1st
and 2nd degrees. Again, this year’s resolution seeks to have the door remain open
after the request and not closed until after the Master has given his permission for
the newly obligated candidate to enter.
In considering the matter, the Ritual Committee weighed both sides of
the argument. The matter was resolved after discussing the purpose and lessons
being taught to BOTH the candidate and the members by the closing of the door,
as well as the status of the newly obligated Brother. In summary: The purpose is
to reinforce the Master’s authority to ensure all is in readiness prior to admitting
the candidate, to reinforce the earlier lessons for the candidate in patience and
reflection, and his status of not yet being a member!
The purpose – first the purpose of closing the door stems from our
heritage of preventing observations of our work by cowans and eavesdroppers.
Consequently, the doors of freemasonry are only open for short durations during
tiled meetings. Secondly, the purpose of closing the door stems from the master’s
authority to personally approve each admission to his lodge and to ensure all
is in readiness prior to the admission. This procedure dictates that the request
for admission and the master’s response be done privately. Although we know
of no instance in which it has happened, circumstances might demand that the
master deny the candidate’s reentry. Suppose, for example, that an objection had
just been raised. This procedure ensures that any visitor, be he a member of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

233

lodge, a visitor from another lodge, a candidate for the degrees, a newly obligated
brother, the grand master or his representative all wait a time with patience as
the master contemplates the appropriateness of the request, and the preparations
necessary for the desired admission. Consequently, the master’s authority to
control his lodge is preserved, and every brother is treated exactly the same, from
the candidate to the grand master.
The lesson - in each degree the candidate is taught a lesson in patience and
reflection. Each time the candidate knocks at the candidate’s door of freemasonry
he is told to “wait a time with patience” and the door closed to allow him to again
be alone with his thoughts, to reflect upon his future, another lesson in patience.
When the candidate returns to the door as a newly obligated brother the closing
of the door after inquiry is yet another opportunity for the candidate to be alone
with his thoughts, to reflect upon his future, and learn another lesson in patience.
His status – we should not forget that the status of the newly obligated
Brother is just that, “newly obligated”. He has not yet completed the entire degree,
thus, not yet entitled to the rights and benefits of that particular degree. In fact, he
does not become a member until he completes the Third Degree. Until then, the
newly obligated Brother is a candidate, who wishes to continue the educational
lessons provided by the involved degree; one of which is the lesson of patience
and reflection learned from behind the closed door.
The first and lasting impressions provided to the candidate are the
importance of faith, patience, and reflection: Faith in the fact that his new Brothers
have his welfare in mind; patience to never act hastily; and his reflection upon
how Masonry will affect his future.
The first and lasting impressions provided to the members are the
equality of all who enter the lodge and the authority of the Master to privately
control its activities.
The ceremonies of our degrees were developed to impress the candidate
and never to offend nor embarrass him. When the candidate comes our doors
for the first time it is with curiosity and trepidation which was soon replaced by
understanding and faith that the brethren have his welfare at heart.
To change the manner in which the newly obligated Brother is admitted
at the start of the second section of the 1st and 2nd Degrees has not proven to be
a burden over the years to the Fraternity in general or the lodge in particular.
Additionally, the proponents have not demonstrated a compelling need to change
the ritual that has been perfected over the years and passed along from generation
to generation; therefore, the Ritual Committee does not support this resolution.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.

Resolution No. 12-16
Requires Biographies of Candidates in Grand Lodge Elections

The proponents of this Resolution seek to provide a procedure for Grand Lodge
elective officer nominations from the floor.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Sections 404.420 and 404.430 of the California Masonic
Code specify that when recommendations for election to the offices of Junior Grand
Warden, Grand Treasurer, Grand Secretary and Grand Lecturer are distributed, a
biographical sketch is attached only for the recommendee for election as Junior
Grand Warden; and
WHEREAS, only the Junior Grand Warden has his biographical sketch
read at Annual Communication; and
WHEREAS, a nominee for any of the elected offices may be made from
the floor; and
WHEREAS, the members of Grand Lodge cannot be expected to make
informed decisions if they do not know the qualifications of multiple nominees.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 404.410 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§404.410. ELECTED OFFICERS.
The Grand Master, Deputy Grand Master, Grand Wardens, Grand Treasurer, Grand
Secretary, and Grand Lecturer shall be elected by written ballot as the final item
of business before the installation of said officers at each Annual Communication.
A majority of the votes cast shall be necessary for an election. Grand Lodge,
by unanimous consent, may permit any designated officer to cast the ballot for
Grand Lodge.
Each recommendee for election to any Grand Lodge office shall provide his
biographical sketch to the Grand Secretary no less than two weeks prior to the
start of Annual Communication. Any other member desiring to be nominated for
election as a Grand Lodge officer may provide his biographical sketch to the Grand
Secretary no less than two weeks prior to the start of Annual Communication.
Nominations for election to any Grand Lodge office shall include only the name
and current title of the nominee. At the conclusion of the nomination process
for each elective office, if there are multiple nominees, the Grand Orator shall
read the biographical sketch submitted for each nominee, if received by him at
least two weeks prior to the start of Annual Communication, in the order of their
nominations. The biographical sketch of the Junior Grand Warden shall be read by

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

235

the Grand Orator whether or not there are multiple nominees. The Grand Orator
shall read only the facts from each biographical sketch. If the Grand Secretary did
not receive a biographical sketch for a nominee by the required date, the vote shall
be taken without reading a biographical sketch for that nominee.
Each elective officer shall be installed before the close of the Annual
Communication and shall serve until the installation of his successor, subject to
Section 404.510. This installation may be public or private at the option of the
incoming Grand Master.
If an elective officer is unable to be present, due to circumstances beyond his
control, he may be installed by the Grand Master at an appropriate place, with
such ceremony as deemed proper by the Grand Master, as soon as practicable
not to exceed 60 days. If the elective officer is not installed within 60 days, the
office shall be declared vacant and the Grand Master may appoint any member of
Grand Lodge to fill the vacant elective office temporarily or for the remainder of
the Grand Lodge year.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution 2012-16 seeks to amend Section 404.410 of our California
Masonic Code to provide a procedure for open nominations and for biographical
sketches to be provided for all elected positions of the Grand Lodge.
It is noted that it has been the policy of this Grand Lodge to alternate the
residency of the elected grand line from the north and the south. This requirement
is not addressed in this open nomination process. Also, this Resolution requires
that a biographical sketch be submitted by every elected Grand Lodge Officer.
Although not specifically stated in the California Masonic Code, it has
been the practice of our Grand Master, during elections, to ask for “any other
nominations”. This is consistent with Robert’s Rule of Order, Chapter 12. Also,
during the nomination of the Junior Grand Warden, his biographical sketch is read
by the Grand Secretary.
It is the policy of our Grand Lodge to provide education and information
to the Craft to allow them to be current on the status of the processes of our
Grand Lodge.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Resolution CARRIED-OVER.

Resolution No 12-17
Allows for Electronic Storage of Lodge Records

The proponents of this Resolution seek to permit a Lodge to maintain its older
records in electronically recorded form.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, current Masonic law requires the Secretary of a Lodge to
maintain all of its books and records; and
WHEREAS, all books and records of a Lodge must be kept in
perpetuity; and
WHEREAS, the paperwork generated in the ordinary course of Lodge
business may become voluminous, thereby making it difficult to maintain the
same in original form; and
WHEREAS, technology has advanced to such a degree that Lodge
records may be recorded in permanent format without the necessity of keeping
original Lodge records in storage.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 805.230 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§805.230. DUTIES OF SECRETARY.
It shall be the duty of the Secretary to:
A.

Record all proceedings at each meeting proper to be written, under the
direction of the Master, and to transcribe the same in a minute book
to be kept for that purpose, and at the next Stated Meeting to read the
minutes to the Lodge and, after they are approved, to present them to the
Master for his signature. After approval no change may be made except
by appropriate motion properly recorded;

B.

Present to the Lodge at each August Stated Meeting, a statement of
income and expenditures, assets and liabilities, on a form promulgated
by the Grand Master, for the six months ended on the preceding June
30th, and at each February Stated Meeting a similar statement for the
12 months ended on the preceding December 31st. The Secretary shall
submit a copy of this 12 month statement to the Inspector of the district
to which the Lodge is assigned and to the Grand Master on or before the
following March 15th;

C.

Prepare and transmit a copy of such record, or of any part thereof, to
Grand Lodge, when required;

Receive all monies due the Lodge, and pay the same monthly or more
frequently as necessary, to the Treasurer; or shall deposit the same not

deposit tags or receipts therefor, one to be immediately delivered to the
Treasurer, the other to be kept by the Secretary as a voucher;

E.

this Code;

F.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

239

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to amend the California Masonic
Code to permit a Lodge to store records more than five years old in electronic
form and discard the originals.
During the past decade great changes have occurred in the way in which
businesses and other organizations maintain their records. Most documents are
originally created in electronic form and many are never printed. In 2001, the
Grand Lodge of California began distributing the proceedings of each annual
communication in electronic form, with a printed copy available on request. The
Grand Master’s itinerary was once printed and distributed to each Lodge; now it
is available on the Grand Lodge web site.
However, one of the drawbacks of maintaining records in electronic
form is the change in format that may occur over time. For example, documents
created twenty years ago using then state-of-the-art word processing software are
only readable today after running a converter tool. Opening a Word Document file
in a version of Word other than the one with which it was created can sometimes
cause incorrect display of the document.
This Resolution addresses that issue by requiring that all electronic
records be maintained in retrievable form, which imposes an implicit requirement
that the electronic format of old records be updated by the Secretary to maintain
compatibility with the latest software.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Resolution ADOPTED.
Resolution No. 12-18
Requires Member Consent to Publish Personal Information to the Public
The proponents of this Resolution seek to require a member to give his consent
before his personal information may be published to the public.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, we live in an age of internet connectivity that presents
threats including identity theft; and
WHEREAS, personal information about ourselves, combined with our
commitment to aide one another, could when injected into the public domain
present an enticing target for criminals and con artists; and
WHEREAS, Freemasons are still persecuted in parts of the world and
some must travel to those places; and

240

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, many members are law enforcement or correctional
officers whose identity, contact information and residences if know by criminals
may make them and their families targets of aggression and criminal acts by
individuals and gangs.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 810.040 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§810.040. LODGE PUBLICATIONS.
A Lodge may publish and mail a Lodge bulletin informing the members of the
Lodge of its activities and including news items relating to any of the Masonic
Organizations so as to promote Masonic intercourse. The bulletin may be a joint
publication of the Lodge and one or more other Lodges and Masonic Organizations
if each participating organization pays its prorata share of the cost to publish and
mail the bulletin. However, the sponsors of a joint publication may permit any
Masonic Youth Order to include material in the publication without charge, and
the sponsors may assume the cost of mailing the publication to members of the
Masonic Youth Order.
The foregoing notwithstanding, no Lodge may publish in the public domain
any personally identifying information about a Mason of the Lodge without the
affirmative written consent from that Mason.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 810.050 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§810.050. LODGE ROSTERS.
A Lodge may publish a roster for Masonic purposes and for the benefit of its
Masons containing the names, mailing addresses and telephone numbers of all
of its Masons. A Lodge may also include in its published roster an electronic
mail address for a Mason of the Lodge with his permission. However, no Lodge
may publish in the public domain any personally identifying information about
a Mason of the Lodge without the affirmative written consent from that Mason.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to require a member to give
his consent before his personal information may be published to the public.
This Resolution specifies that no Lodge may publish in the public domain any
personally identifying information about a Mason of the Lodge without the
consent of that person.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

241

Section 810.040 of the California Masonic Code specifies that bulletins
published by Lodges are to inform members of the Lodge of its activities.
Section 810.050 of the California Masonic Code specifies that Lodge rosters
are for the benefit of its members containing names, mailing addresses and
telephone numbers. Email addresses may be included if the member has given
his permission.
Resolution Number 2010-12 would have expanded Lodge rosters to
include such information as spouses names, birth dates, anniversary dates, etc.
The report of this committee on that Resolution included the concern for identity
theft and privacy issues, and that Resolution failed to pass.
While the Appendix on Grand Masters’ Decisions titled “Use of Social
Networks and Websites 2009 Grand Master’s Decision No 4” states that a
Lodge, a Masonic group and a Mason may have a presence on social networking
sites like Facebook and Myspace, it does not include rosters of any kind.
Protection against identity theft and privacy should always be a concern
and it has long been the policy of this Grand Lodge to maintain the privacy of
its members.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Resolution CARRIED-OVER.

Report of the President of the Board
Masonic Homes of California
July 2011-June 2012
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F & A.M. of California:
Your Masonic Homes is committed to assisting California Freemasons
and their families with the challenges that they face in today’s fast paced world.
This means a commitment to excellence in the care and services we provide
today, and a thorough and thoughtful examination of the needs of California
Freemasons tomorrow.
Our primary focus is our two retirement communities in Union City and
Covina where our philosophy of care is focused on wellness and quality of life.
We believe that growth does not end at retirement. We believe we can continue
to grow as Masons and contributors to our fraternity and to the community. Both
locations continue to be full of happy brothers and their ladies who are enjoying
their retirement years.
In addition to our residential services, we offer Masonic Outreach
Service. MOS is our effort to help to keep our brothers, their wives or widows
in their homes and/or communities. MOS provides case management to each of
our clients and financial assistance for those whose needs are greater than their
means. MOS has kept hundreds of Masons, wives and widows in their homes. The
Homes sends all widows a free copy of the California Freemason that includes
information on what services are available to them. We encourage each lodge to
keep track of your widows and make sure that their address information is in the
I-Member, so that Masonic Homes can keep them connected to the fraternity.
The Masonic Homes doesn’t just help our oldest members; we also
provide services to Masons under 60 and their families thru Masonic Family
Outreach Service. MFOS was launched in response to brothers affected by the
severe economic downturn and to help Masonic Children with special needs all
across the state. We provide referrals for Masonic families in need, help with
accessing services, and temporary financial assistance to bridge brothers in need
from their current state to self-sufficiency. On average Masonic Family Outreach
has been serving between 15 and 20 Masonic Families each month.
The Masonic Homes has been helping children for over one hundred
years. Over the years the Masonic Homes has been frustrated with the inconsistent
results from varies methods used to diagnose children with emotional and behavior
issues. The Homes joined forces with experts to come up with a comprehensive
method to combine the different disciplines that treat children into one diagnostic
regime with the hope that it will identify all of the issues impacting the child.
As a result, in 2011, the Masonic Homes opened a cutting edge diagnostic and
treatment center called the Masonic Center for Youth and Families.

248

Proceedings of the

The plan includes a detail study of the program and its results to see
if the new diagnostic tools perform better than those in current use. The whole
program and study are off to a great start. There are already many success stories
and a great deal of interest from around the world in the Masonic Center for Youth
and Families. We expect the study to take as long as five years to complete. It is a
cutting edge effort by the Homes to make a difference in children’s lives and the
Masonic Homes is being recognized as a leader in this field.
The financial stability of the Masonic Homes continues to be good.
Again this year, the Homes AA credit rating was reviewed and reaffirmed by the
major credit rating firms. We are in the middle of the five-year plan to deal with
the fall out of the 2009 financial crisis. We are exceeding the plan’s projections
and do not expect any problems in meeting all of our financial obligations. Please
see the report of the Finance Committee for more detailed information.
The Masonic Homes continues to build for the future. Our strategic
planning efforts are looking at improving our MOS program with the Care at
Home concept. The concept behind Care at Home is to deliver quality services
to seniors in their Homes. So rather than simply arrange services under the case
management of Masonic Outreach Program, we will be investigating the feasibility
of delivering those services, either ourselves or through qualified providers that
we contract with throughout the state. I will be able to give you more information
next year as the concept develops.
We are also looking at our whole memory care program to see how we
can improve it, not only for our residents but for our members across the state. We
are looking at new ideas on how to slow down the loss of memory, how to keep a
person with memory issues with their family and in their home longer with better
support programs, and how to help them maintain their dignity and quality of life
despite their condition. Our goal is to keep them connected to their families and
world around them. The Masonic Homes is committed to be a leader in this field.
The last strategic initiative is Lodge Outreach which is an effort to
improve communication and coordination with lodges as we provide services on
behalf of the lodge to its members. We are currently testing these ideas in a pilot
program in the San Diego area. Look for more info on all of these strategic efforts
in the months ahead.
During the year, the Board of Trustees of Masonic Homes of California,
along with the other boards and major committees of Masons of California, began
investigation of Policy Governance, a model of board governance developed by
John Carver. We underwent initial training in February, and much of our annual
board planning retreat in May was dedicated to developing the structures needed
to implement. We are planning a special board meeting in July to complete that
work and formally consider adoption of the new model.

Report of the Admissions Committee
Masonic Homes of California
July 2011-June 2012

The Admission Review Program of the Board is a carefully developed
analysis and evaluation process that continues to be improved and refined to meet
the evolving needs to our Applicants, as well as the Homes Staff and the Board.
The interview process and on site evaluation is done at the same time
the applicant visits one of the two facilities. A Staff report on this overnight visit,
together with the Medical Director’s comments on his/her review of the medical
information, is then added to the application. The staff then develops an executive
summary on the applicants and presents that to the Admission Committee for
review and approval. Anytime the Staff recommends against admission the
full application is given to the Admission Committee for detailed review and
discussion during the Admission Committee meeting. Any recommendation
against admission requires the full Board confirmation.
Prior to the regular Admission Committee meeting on the second
Tuesday of each month, the three Trustees, who form the Admission Committee,
each receive and carefully study the complete applications not recommended
for Masonic assistance and the executive summaries for applications
recommended for Masonic assistance. Each Trustee reviews and evaluates the
applications and accompanying data and then discusses his viewpoint during
the Admission Committee meeting. Home’s Staff and the Administrators attend
Admissions Committee meeting to answer committee member’s questions and
to provide additional information to the committee members. The committee’s
recommendations and comments are then presented to the full Board
for confirmation.
The number of applications handled by the Admission Committee varies
from month to month. From July 1, 2011 to June 30, 2012, 49 have been admitted
to both campuses. Union City currently has 256 residents, including the 11
residents in the Traditions Special Care Unit. Covina currently has 77 residents.
For this time period we had 81 applications completed by our brothers, widows,
and mothers.
The Masonic Outreach Services department continues to grow and has
two effective programs in assisting our eligible Brethren and their families or
widows. MFOS is our Masonic Family Outreach Service program that supports
our eligible Brethren under sixty years of age and MSOS is our Masonic
Senior Outreach Service program that supports our Brethren over years of age.
These programs provide the necessary support, financial, housing and/or care
management assistance to applicants who are in need of this type of support to
remain in their present community or residence. The Masonic Outreach Services

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

251

program is currently serving the need of 238 total clients. This year the committee
has reviewed and approved a total of 59 applications for this program. Members
of the staff monitor those individuals, in both programs, on a regular basis to
ensure that their needs are being met.
I want to thank the other Trustees of the Admission Committee who
labor long and hard over the applications. They are Richard Hopper, PGM and
Stuart Wright. I would also like to express my appreciation to the Administrators
and Executive Directors of Covina and Union City Homes as well as their staff,
the continued dedication of the Masonic Outreach Staff to the applicants and the
Board of Trustees.
Respectfully submitted,

Report of the Finance Committee
Masonic Homes of California
July 2011-June 2012
It has been an honor for the members of the Finance Committee to serve
your Masonic Homes of California this past year. This committee monitors and
manages the finances for the Masonic Homes of California and is charged with
the important responsibility of ensuring that we serve our residents today, while
protecting our legacy for future generations
The Masonic Homes of California uses a fiscal year ending on October
31st. For the seven months ended May 31, 2012 the Masonic Homes recorded an
unaudited surplus of income over expenses of $871,000. This result represents
a favorable variance from budget of $857,000, and was achieved primarily by
bringing in expenses below budget.
Operating expenditures of MHC have been guided by the Investment
Distribution Policy. This policy is set as a percentage of a five-year rolling
average of the General and Endowment Funds’ market value. This approach
insures our operating budget will be somewhat buffered from year-to-year market
swings while protecting the integrity of the fund balances for future generations
of residents. The Finance Committee reaffirmed its recommendation to the Board,
first approved two years ago, to reduce the distribution from the General and
Endowment Funds to 4.25%, well below the historical distribution of 5% and even
below the cautionary recommendation of the Investment Committee, which had
recommended a distribution of 4.5%. This Committee is committed to constantly

252

Proceedings of the

re-evaluating the operations of the Homes to ensure we are operating efficiently,
all the while maintaining the highest level of care and resident satisfaction. In
addition, we continue to explore opportunities to diversify the revenue sources of
the Homes to better protect our assets for future generations.
The Finance Committee reviewed regular reports from the Grand
Treasurer and Chief Financial Officer. These reports include quarterly investment
performance reports, monthly operating statements, quarterly capital project
reviews and various others. Moss Adams, LLP, the auditors for Grand Lodge and
the Masonic Homes, have completed the annual external audit for the fiscal year
ended October 31, 2011, which was reviewed by the Finance Committee. The
audit was unqualified. The Audit for the fiscal year ending October 31, 2012 will
be completed in early 2013. The Committee also reviewed the IRS Form 990 and
the California Franchise Tax Board Form 199 regarding the Masonic Homes.
The Finance Committee will work with management to develop the
fiscal year 2012-13 budget. In the face of ever rising costs, management and the
Finance Committee will carefully consider revenues and expenses, including the
4.25% Investment Distribution payout.
The Finance Committee also worked with management to develop a
capital project budget to assure the Homes remain well-maintained and safe to
protect the comfort and safety of our residents. The Homes continues to fund
the Capital Reserve Fund from a percentage of the annual depreciation through
the operating budget. This fund is used to pay for capital projects and to build a
reserve for future needs. The budget developed for FY2013 will allow the balance
in this fund to grow for future capital needs.
During the course of this year, the Committee also oversaw the regular
credit review for Masonic Homes. The Fitch Rating Agency reaffirmed our AA
credit rating, first obtained in 2007. At this writing, we are scheduled for a review
by S & P in late June, 2012, and expect to have news of its rating decision by
late summer.
The above represents the highlights of the committee’s efforts this year. I
